name: Crater
introduction: is the Cup of Apollo, perched on the back of Hydra beside Corvus, the crow that failed to bring it back filled with water. It is a faint bowl of stars, best seen on northern spring evenings.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: Crater’s stars are modest, but beyond them hides one of the strangest galaxies known. Crater II, discovered in 2016, is a satellite of the Milky Way almost as wide as the Large Magellanic Cloud, yet so spread out and faint that it went unnoticed until deep surveys revealed it.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: [Delta Crateris](hip:55282), the brightest star, is an orange giant about 190 light-years away. [Alkes](hip:53740), Alpha Crateris, marks the base of the cup, and [Gamma Crateris](hip:55705) is a white star with a faint companion.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: Crater lies far from the Milky Way, so the view through it reaches distant galaxies rather than nearby star clouds. Many of the faint smudges seen there in deep images are galaxies millions of light-years away.
